title: Concurrent non-queue controller commanded the robot during engineering job 5a482e85
classification: serialization conflict with a transient thermal rise; no tip, brownout, jam, or persistent servo loss
summary: While this job held the guarded handoff for experiment 2ae9157f, a second controller commanded stand/lower on the same robot. It ran from 00:04:38Z to 00:12:11Z, at one point cycling stand and lower about every 8 seconds without waiting for the async motion worker to finish. Knee servo temperatures rose from 34 C to 50 C. The robot ended the episode back at logical zero, level and healthy.

attribution.conclusion: The :8898 RL web hub, driven from a browser inside the Codex desktop app (PID 1211). Not this job, not the Robot Lab service, not a Robot Lab guarded runner.
evidence: linux_control/logs/commands.jsonl seq 2,5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12 record POST /api/rl/stand and /api/rl/lower with body {"tilt_trip_deg": 20} from peer 192.168.4.123.
This job's runner script never executed; only python3 -m py_compile was run on it.
System python3 on this Mac is 3.9.6, so this job cannot be the Python-urllib/3.12 caller.
rl_move/sim/web_hub.py:342 and rl_move/sim/web_server.py:386 proxy /api/rl/stand and /api/rl/lower; that hub runs on python 3.12.14 (PID 70498).
lsof showed PID 70498 as the only process holding a connection to 192.168.4.39:8080, and its :8898 listener had six established connections from PID 1211, the Codex app network service.
grep for 'api/rl/stand' across the installed hexapod_lab package returned nothing, ruling out the Robot Lab service.

timeline_utc.event: This job deployed commit e6b05af1 and the hexapod-web service restarted.
This job POST /api/rl/stop, intended as an abort-path check on a believed-idle robot. It aborted the foreign stand during start-pose acquisition, leaving the robot in the tuck pose.
FOREIGN POST /api/zero {"pose":"sit"}, curl/8.7.1. This is go_zero, a MOVE to the zero pose. It is not set_zero_here, so the zero frame was NOT modified.
FOREIGN stand/lower cycled five more times at roughly 8 s intervals, Python-urllib/3.12 — faster than the async motion worker completes.
FOREIGN POST /api/rl/lower, curl/8.7.1. Last foreign motion command.
Robot Lab reported process standup_step_down 'done · step sit-down peak 2.44 A', busy false.
Seven minutes quiet. Robot at logical zero, all 18 joints within 0.8 deg. Knees cooling 50 -> 48 C.

physical_observations.no_zero_frame_change: No /api/set_zero appears anywhere in the journal; joints read within 0.8 deg of zero afterwards.

knee_temperature_c.note: Persistent and load-correlated across the six knee joints (j2 50, j8 47, j14 42), not the isolated single-sample corruption pattern seen in experiment 922434955b.

physical_observations.tilt: roll stayed within -0.95..0.1 deg and pitch within 1.3..5.0 deg throughout; no tip.
physical_observations.bus: 18/18 motors in every sample, bus never quarantined, no new /api/errors entries.
physical_observations.camera: robot-3 frame at 17:06:22 local shows the chassis upright and low with feet planted and the test area clear.

impact_on_this_job: The saved plan requires the robot to start belly-down at logical zero under exclusive control. That precondition was destroyed twice and then restored by the foreign controller's own final lower.
recommendation: The :8898 RL web hub can command robot motion without passing through the Robot Lab serialized queue or its readiness gate, so it can collide with an in-flight guarded handoff. Robot Lab reported guarded_runner_ready false and can_start_from_website false the whole time, and neither prevented this. Consider making the hub's robot-target motion routes refuse while a guarded handoff is leased, or at least surface the lease in the hub UI.
